note: The rate negotiator.  Its five diagnostics are gated on a LOCAL copy of the level rather than on DSPLIB_DEBUG_ON(), and each one re-reads the variables it printed afterwards -- both are the object's register allocation showing through, and both are mutated below.

label: the cached level is read once and never refreshed
why: nothing between the two reads writes `dsplibs_debug_level` -- `dsplibs_debug_printf` only consumes it -- so the reload cannot yield a different value.  Reproduced because the object emits it: the call clobbers the register the level was living in.

label: the preliminary report does not re-read the two rates
why: `tx` and `rx` already equal `cfg->txbits` and `cfg->rxbits` here -- the clamps above assign the local and the field together -- so re-reading them cannot change either.  Same register reload as the level above.

label: the gate is level >= 1 rather than > 1
the ZERODIV gate is level >= 1 rather than > 1
the preliminary report has tx and rx swapped
the preliminary report gives rates in symbols, not bits
the final report has tx and rx swapped
the final report reads the working copies rather than the config
the nofTxBits report has the rate and the PTC swapped
the nofTxBits report does not re-read its two inputs
why: `bits` and `umax` were read from those same two fields at the top of the block and nothing has written them since, so the reload is a no-op.  Worth reproducing even so: unlike the two above, these values ARE used afterwards, by the initV34 call below, so the reload is load-bearing in the object even though no test can see it here.
